member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.ForceProfile
member.summary: A named, versioned set of every parameter that decides how a game feels: the and the conditioning chain together, as data.

remarks.para: The point of versioning is that a tune can be swapped without rebuilding a game and without losing the one it replaced. A consumer names a profile (arcade-outrun@1); to try a different feel you add a new version, point the game's config at it, and drive both. Comparing two builds is how tuning stops being reproducible.

A published version is immutable. Editing arcade-outrun@1 makes every earlier report about it a lie, including the one in the case file. Add @2 instead; inherits keeps that to the lines that actually changed.
The same files are parsed by native/forcemodel/force_profile.h, and a conformance test pins the two readers to identical results. Add a key in one and you must add it in the other.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.ForceShaper
member.summary: The output conditioning chain every wheel mod ends up writing: deadzone, dual-rate smoothing, gain, soft saturation, slew limiting with event bypass, low-speed fade, warm-up ramp and inversion. Pure math, no device.
member.remarks: Order matters and is fixed (see knowledge/FFB-SIGNAL-DESIGN.md): deadzone → EMA → gain/invert → soft saturation → slew → fade → ramp → clamp. Gain and invert are the boundary: above them the value is in model units, below them in true output units and true output sign, and every stage below is a device-side limit. They moved there in 0.8.0. Applied last, gain re-inflated an already-saturated value into the hard clamp - above about Strength 65 the slew limiter then latched the output at full scale in whichever direction it first clipped, and the model could not recover it. Invert applied last gave the slew limiter a _last of the opposite sign, so with Invert on a steady input oscillated near zero and no force ever arrived. Structural force goes through all of it; an isEvent update (crash impulse, shift pulse) bypasses the EMA and slew so it arrives as a pulse rather than a shove. Rules lifted from OutRun2006Tweaks-FFB (chain), art-of-sim-rally (fade, Strength as the only dial) and cruisn-collection (slew and clamp as the instability ladder).

Use it when your own input layer has already chosen a device: two Fanatec devices can carry the same name, so matching by name is guesswork exactly where it hurts. Null clears it. Toolkit 0.2.0+.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.CreatePeriodic(System.Int32)
member.summary: Creates a hardware sine effect (road texture, tyre slip) on the held wheel, initially silent. Returns the slot for , or -1 when the driver has no periodic support - then synthesise at 15 Hz or below through instead. Toolkit 0.2.0+.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.UpdatePeriodic(System.Int32,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Envelope update; safe to call every frame (unchanged envelopes never reach the driver).

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.CreateConstantBurst(System.Int32)
member.summary: Allocate an idle independent constant slot, duration 1..500 ms. Native 0.8.0.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.PlayConstantBurst(System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: One finite signed constant pulse [-1,1]. Zero stops. Never stops steering. Acceptance is not measured torque or combined-output headroom. Do not retry stale events.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.CreatePeriodicBurst(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Create an idle sine burst (1..100 Hz, 1..500 ms), or -1 on failure. Shares four slots with continuous periodics. Requires native component 0.6.0.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.PlayPeriodicBurst(System.Int32,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Explicitly restart one finite burst. True means the native play was accepted, not proof of physical output. Zero stops. Failed events must not be queued/retried. Every positive magnitude maps to at least one device unit; no 5% change gate.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.PlayShapedPeriodicBurst(System.Int32,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Finite sine with explicit phase and a fade to zero over the final fadeMs. True means exact API parameter readback and start accepted, not physical verification. Missing optional export returns false; failed events must not be retried.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.StopPeriodicBurst(System.Int32)
member.summary: Stop a valid burst slot, including an already stopped slot. Retains the slot. ReleasePeriodics frees all continuous and burst slots. May stop while FFB is not Ready.

member.name: M:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.CreateCondition(Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative.ConditionKind)
member.summary: Creates a hardware condition effect - the base computes force from axis position or velocity continuously, rather than following our updates. A hardware damper is smoother and more stable than damping synthesised at 60 Hz, and is usually the right answer to a base that oscillates. Returns the slot, or -1 when the driver has no such effect (normal; fall back to damping in the model). Toolkit 0.4.0+.

member.summary: Updates a condition slot. All four are -1..1 (saturation and deadband 0..1); safe to call every frame, since an unchanged condition never reaches the driver.
